lsty-05-c2.text: Rebecca Hersher (2016). Christopher Marlowe Officially Credited As Co-Author Of 3 Shakespeare Plays. NPR.

lsty-05-c2.text: Santiago Segarra, Mark Eisen, Alejandro Ribeiro (2014). Authorship Attribution through Function Word Adjacency Networks. arXiv (IEEE Transactions on Signal Processing).

lsty-05-c2.claim: In benchmark tests, attribution accuracy exceeded that of methods based on word frequencies alone, and combining the two did better still.

lsty-05-c3.text: Rebecca Hersher (2016). Christopher Marlowe Officially Credited As Co-Author Of 3 Shakespeare Plays. NPR.

lsty-05-c3.claim: Carol Rutter of the University of Warwick told the BBC she would be very surprised if Marlowe was one of Shakespeare's collaborators.

lsty-05-c3.text: Ros Barber (2020). Function Word Adjacency Networks and Early Modern Plays. ANQ: A Quarterly Journal of Short Articles, Notes and Reviews.
lsty-05-c3.quote: The Word Adjacency Network method underpinning the New Oxford Shakespeare’s attribution of the Henry VI plays to Christopher Marlowe as co-author has not been independently tested
lsty-05-c3.claim: In 2020 Ros Barber argued that the word adjacency method behind the attribution had not been independently tested, that sections designated as Shakespeare's were often not detected as his by the method's own definitions, and that its high claimed success rates rested on a flawed validation process known as overfitting.

lsty-05-c3.text: Kiernan Ryan (2003). Verily a flea in the ear for all who fail to properly hear. Times Higher Education.

lsty-06-c1.text: Arjuna Tuzzi, Michele A. Cortelazzo (eds) (2018). Drawing Elena Ferrante's Profile. Padova University Press.
lsty-06-c1.quote: Elena Ferrante is an internationally acclaimed Italian novelist whose real identity has been kept secret by E/O publishing house for more than 25 years.
lsty-06-c1.claim: Her small Rome-based publisher, Edizioni e/o, kept her real identity secret for more than 25 years.

lsty-06-c1.text: Claudio Gatti (2016). Elena Ferrante: An Answer?. The New York Review of Books.
lsty-06-c1.quote: In fact, in a letter included in Frantumaglia, Ferrante warns her publisher that she will not tell the truth about herself
lsty-06-c1.claim: Ferrante gave interviews through the publisher and gathered letters, interviews and autobiographical writing in Frantumaglia, while warning there that she would lie when necessary to shield herself.

lsty-06-c1.text: Claudio Gatti (2016). Elena Ferrante: An Answer?. The New York Review of Books.
lsty-06-c1.quote: new revelations from real estate and financial records point to Anita Raja, a Rome-based translator whose German-born mother fled the Holocaust and later married a Neapolitan magistrate.
lsty-06-c1.claim: Real-estate records and payments from the publisher, he argued, pointed to Anita Raja, a Rome-based translator of German literature who had worked with Edizioni e/o for many years and is married to the novelist Domenico Starnone.

lsty-06-c1.text: Claudio Gatti (2016). Elena Ferrante: An Answer?. The New York Review of Books.
lsty-06-c1.quote: In 2014, Raja’s compensation increased by almost 50 percent, and in 2015 it grew again by more than 150 percent, reaching an amount that was about seven times what she received in 2010
lsty-06-c1.claim: In 2014 Raja's compensation increased by almost 50%, and in 2015 it grew by more than 150%, to about seven times what she had received in 2010, closely tracking the publisher's Ferrante-driven revenues.

lsty-06-c1.text: Claudio Gatti (2016). Elena Ferrante: An Answer?. The New York Review of Books.
lsty-06-c1.quote: A decade ago, at the request of Italian writer Luigi Galella, a team of physicists and mathematicians at La Sapienza University in Rome analyzed Ferrante’s books with special text analysis software.
lsty-06-c1.claim: A decade before, at the request of the writer Luigi Galella, physicists and mathematicians at La Sapienza University in Rome had concluded there was a high probability that Starnone wrote the books.

lsty-06-c1.text: Claudio Gatti (2016). Elena Ferrante: An Answer?. The New York Review of Books.
lsty-06-c1.quote: Neither Raja nor Starnone responded to repeated requests for comment
lsty-06-c1.claim: The publisher Sandro Ferri called such an article an invasion of privacy, both the publishers' and Ferrante's, and neither Raja nor Starnone responded to Gatti's requests for comment.

lsty-06-c2.text: Arjuna Tuzzi, Michele A. Cortelazzo (eds) (2018). Drawing Elena Ferrante's Profile. Padova University Press.
lsty-06-c2.quote: In 2016, Arjuna Tuzzi and Michele Cortelazzo led an Italian research team that conducted a preliminary study and collected a well-founded, large corpus of Italian novels comprising 150 works published in the last 30 years by 40 different authors.
lsty-06-c2.claim: In 2016 Arjuna Tuzzi and Michele Cortelazzo, at the University of Padua, built a corpus of 150 Italian novels published in the previous 30 years by 40 different authors, chosen with the main hypotheses about Ferrante in mind.

lsty-06-c2.text: Arjuna Tuzzi, Michele A. Cortelazzo (eds) (2018). Drawing Elena Ferrante's Profile. Padova University Press.
lsty-06-c2.quote: first presented during the international workshop Drawing Elena Ferrante’s Profile in Padua on 7 September 2017
lsty-06-c2.claim: Maciej Eder and Jan Rybicki, Patrick Juola, Vittorio Loreto's team, George Mikros, Pierre Ratinaud and Jacques Savoy all took part, and the results were presented at the workshop Drawing Elena Ferrante's Profile in Padua on 7 September 2017.

lsty-06-c2.text: Arjuna Tuzzi, Michele A. Cortelazzo (2018). It Takes Many Hands to Draw Elena Ferrante's Profile. Drawing Elena Ferrante's Profile: Workshop Proceedings (Padova University Press).
lsty-06-c2.quote: The novelist coming closest to Elena Ferrante, and consequently the most similar in terms of their lexical profiles, is Domenico Starnone.
lsty-06-c2.claim: The novelist closest to her lexical profile was Domenico Starnone, and the similarity held when they measured distance using grammatical words only, so it was not a matter of shared settings or plots.

lsty-06-c2.text: Jacques Savoy (2018). Elena Ferrante Unmasked. Drawing Elena Ferrante's Profile: Workshop Proceedings (Padova University Press).
lsty-06-c2.quote: For all these 7 (novels) x 7 (feature sets) x 2 (tokens or lemmas) = 98 experiments, the same name appears in the first rank: Domenico Starnone.
lsty-06-c2.claim: Savoy ran Delta on each of Ferrante's seven novels with seven sizes of feature set, on both word forms and lemmas: 98 experiments, with Starnone ranked first every time.

lsty-06-c2.text: Maciej Eder (2018). Elena Ferrante: A Virtual Author. Drawing Elena Ferrante's Profile: Workshop Proceedings (Padova University Press).
lsty-06-c2.quote: The picture for all the remaining novels by Ferrante turned out to be simply identical: with no single exception all the segments in all of these novels were ascribed to Starnone.
lsty-06-c2.claim: With no single exception, every segment of every Ferrante novel was ascribed to Starnone.

lsty-06-c2.text: Patrick Juola (2018). Thesaurus-Based Semantic Similarity Judgments: A New Approach to Authorial Similarity?. Drawing Elena Ferrante's Profile: Workshop Proceedings (Padova University Press).
lsty-06-c2.quote: Of the thirty-nine distractor authors, only two (Murgia and Starnone) had no significant differences in concept usage when compared with Ferrante.
lsty-06-c2.claim: Of 39 distractor authors, only Michela Murgia and Starnone showed no significant differences from Ferrante.

lsty-06-c2.text: Patrick Juola (2018). Thesaurus-Based Semantic Similarity Judgments: A New Approach to Authorial Similarity?. Drawing Elena Ferrante's Profile: Workshop Proceedings (Padova University Press).
lsty-06-c2.quote: If we allow none-of-the-above as a possible response, then all that has been shown is that Ferrante is someone who writes like Starnone and Murgia.
lsty-06-c2.claim: This is a closed-set result: if you allow none of the above as an answer, all that has been shown is that Ferrante writes like Starnone and Murgia.

lsty-06-c3.text: Maciej Eder (2018). Elena Ferrante: A Virtual Author. Drawing Elena Ferrante's Profile: Workshop Proceedings (Padova University Press).
lsty-06-c3.quote: works written collaboratively by Hildegard and her secretary Guibert of Gembloux form a discrete profile, which is not a simple combination of both Hildegard’s and Guibert’s styles
lsty-06-c3.claim: Works she wrote with her secretary, Guibert of Gembloux, formed a distinct profile that was not a simple mix of the two styles: a virtual third author.

lsty-06-c3.text: Jan Rybicki (2018). Partners in Life, Partners in Crime?. Drawing Elena Ferrante's Profile: Workshop Proceedings (Padova University Press).
lsty-06-c3.quote: And yet there, too, the stylometric signal in the texts was exclusively that of the writer Dehnel – as if Tarczyński had no hand in this, and I know he had (2016).
lsty-06-c3.claim: The stylometric signal was exclusively Dehnel's, although Rybicki knew Tarczyński had taken part.

lsty-06-c3.text: Jan Rybicki (2018). Partners in Life, Partners in Crime?. Drawing Elena Ferrante's Profile: Workshop Proceedings (Padova University Press).
lsty-06-c3.quote: It would be quite plausible that, in the light of all of my three caveats, Ferrante is in fact a joint effort of Raja and Starnone.
lsty-06-c3.claim: Raja's stylometric invisibility, he suggested, might be linked to her profession, and Ferrante could plausibly be a joint effort of Raja and Starnone.

lsty-06-c3.text: Arjuna Tuzzi, Michele A. Cortelazzo (2018). It Takes Many Hands to Draw Elena Ferrante's Profile. Drawing Elena Ferrante's Profile: Workshop Proceedings (Padova University Press).
lsty-06-c3.quote: Our preliminary results suggest that more than one author might have contributed to Ferrante’s collection, seemingly at least one man and one woman, and the author(s) would appear to come from Naples, and be over 60 years old.
lsty-06-c3.claim: Their preliminary results suggested more than one author, seemingly at least one man and one woman, from Naples and over 60 years old; they pointed to Starnone and Raja and seemed to rule out Marmo.

lsty-06-c3.text: Arjuna Tuzzi, Michele A. Cortelazzo (2018). It Takes Many Hands to Draw Elena Ferrante's Profile. Drawing Elena Ferrante's Profile: Workshop Proceedings (Padova University Press).
lsty-06-c3.quote: So, Elena Ferrante’s books may be the work not of a single author, but of some form of cooperation (though what form this may take is not easy to imagine) involving at least two authors
lsty-06-c3.claim: Ferrante's novels are closer in style to Starnone's than to those of any other novelist tested, and the books may be the work of some form of cooperation.

lsty-06-c3.text: Jan Rybicki (2018). Partners in Life, Partners in Crime?. Drawing Elena Ferrante's Profile: Workshop Proceedings (Padova University Press).
lsty-06-c3.quote: In my private opinion, the sensational question of Ferrante’s identity – although it may continue to make headlines in international press – is infinitely less important than that of the creative act of writing novels
lsty-06-c3.claim: Rybicki, who took part, wrote that in his private opinion the sensational question of identity is infinitely less important than what happens when people write together.

lsty-07-c1.text: Franco Moretti (2000). Conjectures on World Literature. New Left Review.

lsty-07-c1.claim: In his essay Conjectures on World Literature, in New Left Review, he admitted that, as a scholar of West European narrative between 1790 and 1930, he really worked only on its canonical fraction, which is not even one per cent of published literature.

lsty-07-c1.quote: there are thirty thousand nineteenth-century British novels out there, forty, fifty, sixty thousand—no one really knows, no one has read them, no one ever will.
lsty-07-c1.claim: There are thirty thousand nineteenth-century British novels, perhaps forty, fifty or sixty thousand, and no one has read them or ever will.

lsty-07-c1.text: University of Basel. Distant Reading: What do distant readers do differently?. TALES, University of Basel.
lsty-07-c1.quote: What we really need is a little pact with the devil: we know how to read texts, now let’s learn how not to read them.
lsty-07-c1.claim: Moretti proposed instead a little pact with the devil: we know how to read texts, now let us learn how not to read them.

lsty-07-c1.text: University of Basel. Distant Reading: What do distant readers do differently?. TALES, University of Basel.
lsty-07-c1.quote: Distant reading: where distance, let me repeat it, is a condition of knowledge: it allows you to focus on units that are much smaller or much larger than the text
lsty-07-c1.claim: in which distance is a condition of knowledge, letting you study units much smaller or much larger than the text

lsty-07-c1.text: Sarah Allison, Ryan Heuser, Matthew Jockers, Franco Moretti, Michael Witmore (2011). Quantitative Formalism: an Experiment. Pamphlets of the Stanford Literary Lab.
lsty-07-c1.quote: The answer is, fundamentally, Yes: but a Yes with so many complications that it is necessary to look at the entire process of our study.
lsty-07-c1.claim: Their answer was fundamentally yes, but with many complications.

lsty-07-c1.text: Sarah Allison, Ryan Heuser, Matthew Jockers, Franco Moretti, Michael Witmore (2011). Quantitative Formalism: an Experiment. Pamphlets of the Stanford Literary Lab.
lsty-07-c1.quote: With Dickens, Brontë, and Eliot, for instance – who had all written both industrial novels and Bildungsroman – the “pull” of the author in figure 6.3 was clearly much stronger than that of the genre
lsty-07-c1.claim: Yet in the novels they kept running into the author signal: for Dickens, Brontë and Eliot, the pull of the author was much stronger than the pull of the genre.

lsty-07-c1.text: Nan Z. Da (2019). The Computational Case against Computational Literary Studies. Critical Inquiry.
lsty-07-c1.quote: The problem with computational literary analysis is that the insights it produces are either robust and obvious or not obvious and not robust
lsty-07-c1.claim: In Critical Inquiry in 2019, Nan Z. Da argued that computational literary analysis produces insights that are either robust and obvious or not obvious and not robust.

lsty-07-c1.text: Paul Barrett (2025). Unjust Readings: Against the New New Criticism. Digital Humanities Quarterly.
lsty-07-c1.quote: they just dress up garden variety literary intuition in numbers
lsty-07-c1.claim: Stanley Fish added that such projects dress up literary intuition in numbers.

lsty-07-c2.text: Baixiang Huang, Canyu Chen, Kai Shu (2024). Can Large Language Models Identify Authorship?. arXiv.
lsty-07-c2.quote: These methods, which typically require fine-tuning on labeled data, often suffer from performance degradation in cross-domain applications and provide limited explainability.
lsty-07-c2.claim: Traditional studies depend on hand-crafted stylistic features, and state-of-the-art approaches use text embeddings from pretrained language models, but these typically need fine-tuning on labelled data, often degrade when moved to a new domain, and explain little.

lsty-07-c2.text: Baixiang Huang, Canyu Chen, Kai Shu (2024). Can Large Language Models Identify Authorship?. arXiv.
lsty-07-c2.quote: Our assessment demonstrates LLMs' proficiency in both tasks without the need for domain-specific fine-tuning, providing explanations into their decision making via a detailed analysis of linguistic features.
lsty-07-c2.claim: The study found LLMs proficient at both zero-shot verification and attribution among 10 or 20 candidate authors, and guiding them with explicit linguistic features let them explain their decisions.

lsty-07-c2.text: Baixiang Huang, Canyu Chen, Kai Shu (2024). Authorship Attribution in the Era of LLMs: Problems, Methodologies, and Challenges. arXiv.
lsty-07-c2.quote: This survey systematically explores the landscape of this field by categorizing four representative problems: (1) Human-written Text Attribution; (2) LLM-generated Text Detection; (3) LLM-generated Text Attribution; and (4) Human-LLM Co-authored Text Attribution.
lsty-07-c2.claim: The same authors' survey sorts the new landscape into four problems: attributing human-written text, detecting LLM-generated text, attributing LLM-generated text, and attributing text that humans and LLMs wrote together.

lsty-07-c2.text: James O'Sullivan (2025). Stylometric comparisons of human versus AI-generated creative writing. Humanities and Social Sciences Communications.
lsty-07-c2.quote: This study employs stylometry to compare the creative writing styles of humans and large language models (LLMs) such as GPT-3.5, GPT-4, and Llama 70b.
lsty-07-c2.claim: James O'Sullivan of University College Cork used Burrows's Delta on short stories written to the same prompts by people and by GPT-3.5, GPT-4 and Llama 70B, in a study published in 2025.

lsty-07-c2.text: University College Cork (2025). New study reveals that AI cannot fully write like a human. UCC News.
lsty-07-c2.quote: AI systems like GPT-3.5, GPT-4, and Llama 70B produce tightly grouped clusters, each reflecting the uniform patterns typical of a given model.
lsty-07-c2.claim: The models' stories formed tight clusters, each with the uniform pattern of its own model, while the human stories were far more varied.

lsty-07-c2.text: University College Cork (2025). New study reveals that AI cannot fully write like a human. UCC News.
lsty-07-c2.quote: GPT-4 writes with even more consistency than GPT-3.5, but both remain distinct from human work.
lsty-07-c2.claim: GPT-4 wrote with even more consistency than GPT-3.5, which only rarely came close to human style.

lsty-07-c2.text: Nasser A Alsadhan (2026). Decoding AI Authorship: Can LLMs Truly Mimic Human Style Across Literature and Politics?. arXiv.
lsty-07-c2.quote: Results demonstrate that AI-generated mimicry remains highly detectable, with XGBoost models trained on a restricted set of eight stylometric features achieving accuracy comparable to high-dimensional neural classifiers.
lsty-07-c2.claim: The imitations remained highly detectable: a classifier trained on just eight stylometric features matched the accuracy of high-dimensional neural classifiers, and perplexity was the most discriminating feature.

lsty-07-c3.text: Mark Hachman (2023). OpenAI's ChatGPT is too good for its own AI to detect. PCWorld.
lsty-07-c3.quote: As of July 20, 2023, the AI classifier is no longer available due to its low rate of accuracy.
lsty-07-c3.claim: OpenAI withdrew its own AI text classifier on 20 July 2023, citing its low rate of accuracy.

lsty-07-c3.text: Weixin Liang, Mert Yuksekgonul, Yining Mao, Eric Wu, James Zou (2023). GPT detectors are biased against non-native English writers. Patterns.
lsty-07-c3.quote: In our study, we evaluated the performance of seven widely used GPT detectors on 91 TOEFL (Test of English as a Foreign Language) essays from a Chinese forum and 88 US eighth-grade essays from the Hewlett Foundation’s ASAP dataset.
lsty-07-c3.claim: Weixin Liang and colleagues tested seven widely used detectors on 91 TOEFL essays by non-native English speakers and 88 essays by US eighth-graders.

lsty-07-c3.text: Weixin Liang, Mert Yuksekgonul, Yining Mao, Eric Wu, James Zou (2023). GPT detectors are biased against non-native English writers. Patterns.
lsty-07-c3.quote: While the detectors accurately classified the US student essays, they incorrectly labeled more than half of the TOEFL essays as "AI-generated" (average false-positive rate: 61.3%).
lsty-07-c3.claim: The detectors classified the US essays accurately but labelled more than half the TOEFL essays as AI-generated, with an average false-positive rate of 61.3%.

lsty-07-c3.text: Kalpesh Krishna, Yixiao Song, Marzena Karpinska, John Wieting, Mohit Iyyer (2023). Paraphrasing evades detectors of AI-generated text, but retrieval is an effective defense. arXiv.
lsty-07-c3.quote: For example, DIPPER drops detection accuracy of DetectGPT from 70.3% to 4.6% (at a constant false positive rate of 1%), without appreciably modifying the input semantics.
lsty-07-c3.claim: Paraphrasing AI text with it cut DetectGPT's detection accuracy from 70.3% to 4.6%, at a false-positive rate of 1%, without appreciably changing the meaning, and it also evaded watermarking and other detectors.

lsty-07-c3.text: John Kirchenbauer, Jonas Geiping, Yuxin Wen, Jonathan Katz, Ian Miers, Tom Goldstein (2023). A Watermark for Large Language Models. arXiv.
lsty-07-c3.quote: The watermark works by selecting a randomized set of "green" tokens before a word is generated, and then softly promoting use of green tokens during sampling.
lsty-07-c3.claim: which softly nudges a model towards a secret, randomised set of green tokens

lsty-07-c3.text: University College Cork (2025). New study reveals that AI cannot fully write like a human. UCC News.
lsty-07-c3.quote: Stylometry can reveal broad patterns across large bodies of text, but it has no place in judging authorship in education.
lsty-07-c3.claim: O'Sullivan, whose own study separated people from models, insists that stylometry has no place in judging authorship in education, because students' writing shifts with task, context and support.
